messages:
elena: FYI P1 from ACME: they see intermittent streaming sessions that start returning 200s but immediately get counted as 5xx in billing and alerting. Ticket #INC-4521. sample logs pasted below.

sam: Can you drop the ticket link + a sample request_id and any graph snapshots?

elena: Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4521. request_id=req_0a1b2c3d. Graph: https://grafana/internal/d/streams/stream-errors?var-customer=acme (spike at 10:12-10:18). Logs:
```
gateway: accept conn from 10.4.5.6
proxy: upstream req req_0a1b2c3d start streaming
nginx-access: 10.4.5.6 - - [17/Mar/2026:10:12:33 +0000] "POST /v1/streams HTTP/1.1" 200 0 "-" "acme-sdk/1.2"
gateway: write to client failed: write tcp 10.4.5.6:52344->1.2.3.4:443: write: broken pipe
router: mark request req_0a1b2c3d as 5xx: EPIPE
```

elena: customer says their mobile SDK may be dropping sockets aggressively (they're on flaky mobile network). They expect these to be classified as client-abort and not gateway 5xx.

dave: That nginx line with body bytes=0 + broken pipe suggests the client closed after headers. We currently treat mid-stream TCP resets and EPIPE as gateway errors. Might need to distinguish FIN from RST and from a proxied half-close.

maria: Do we have tcpdump or SYN/FIN flags from the gateway for that request? Could confirm if client sent FIN before we encountered error.

elena: I pulled tcpdump for the 10:12 window, attached pcaps to the ticket. Quick snippet:
```
10:12:33.102 IP 192.0.2.55.52344 > 198.51.100.10.443: Flags [P.], seq 100:256, ack 1, win 64240
10:12:33.203 IP 198.51.100.10.443 > 192.0.2.55.52344: Flags [.], ack 157
10:12:33.204 IP 192.0.2.55.52344 > 198.51.100.10.443: Flags [F.], seq 157, ack 1, win 64240
```

sam: That shows a FIN from client -> we should treat as client-close. Why is the router marking as 5xx? Is the classification logic misreading EPIPE from write() as internal error?

dave: Exactly. Current pseudo-code:
```
if write_err != nil {
  if is_timeout(write_err) || is_eof(write_err) {
    classify(5xx)
  }
}
```
We don't check for client-sent FIN explicitly when downstream sends FIN after we've already flushed.

maria: Proposed short-term: add heuristic - if nginx access shows status 200 and bytes_sent==0 and SYN/FIN sequence matches client FIN immediately after headers, mark as client-abort (4xx/no-billing). Long-term: adjust router to consult tcp state or conn-tracer at decision time.

elena: Customer is asking for billing correction for the spike window. We need to: 1) reproduce, 2) if repro ok, roll a mitigation canary, 3) update billing for that window.

sam: Repro steps: here's a minimal local curl flow to simulate a mobile client that closes mid-stream. Run server locally (port 8080) that streams chunked and then kill client after first chunk:
```
# server (node/python) sends headers then chunk then sleep
curl -v -N http://localhost:8080/stream --output - &
# wait for first chunk then kill the curl process to emulate client FIN
pkill -f "curl -v -N"
```
This yields server-side write errors with EPIPE locally.

dave: I'm going to patch the router classification to treat EPIPE following a successful 200 header send + immediate client FIN as client-abort. Will open PR and do a canary to 10%.

support-bot: Escalation INC-4521 -> SRE escalation created: SRE-788. Priority: P1.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline: patch/router-classify-client-abort - canary 10% started at 2026-03-17T10:45:00Z (build bld_7021).

maria: Running smoke tests against canary. Using the curl repro, I hit canary endpoints 20x. Observed no billing-classified 5xx for client-kill reproductions. Sample logs:
```
router: req req_5f6e7a classified client-abort (no-billing)
nginx-access: "POST /v1/streams" 200 0
```

elsa: (typo in my head, ignore)

elena: Great. Can we backfill billing for 10:12-10:18 window for ACME? I'll file billing request once we have canary results and a short writeup.

dave: I'll keep the canary at 10% for 2 hours then expand if no regression. We should also add unit test for tcp FIN sequence and an integration test that kills client mid-stream.

sam: I'll add a short runbook note for support: how to identify client FIN in tcpdump + sample log grep commands. Example grep: `grep req_0a1b2c3d /var/log/router.log | grep EPIPE` then cross-ref tcpdump.

maria: Confirming: after 45m of canary traffic we saw 42 reproductions and 0 misclassified 5xxs. Sending summary to ticket.

elena: Thanks team. I'll mark INC-4521 as "fix deployed to canary, billing review pending" and will follow up once finance approves refund. :thumbsup:

dave: Leaving open until canary expanded and billing update done.

support-bot: INC-4521 status updated: in-progress -> awaiting-billing.
